transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-09
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Riya Kapoor (CTO, Atlas), Evan Brooks (ML Eng), Sofia Marquez (Product)
Recording link: (redacted)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy):
- Kickoff for Atlas HealthTech POC focused on cost/unit economics, benchmark plan, and success criteria for inference at scale.
- Discussed target SLOs: p95 latency ~<250ms for short responses, throughput ~10 req/s per model instance; budget constraint ~$15k/mo for initial pilot.
- Preliminary per-token cost estimates and knobs: hosted per-token baseline, batching and KV caching to reduce effective unit cost; recommended benchmark plan and data needed.
- Next steps: Redwood to send cost model spreadsheet and benchmark harness; Atlas to share prompt set and traffic traces.

Topics covered: success criteria, traffic shape, per-token estimates, batching/caching knobs, private vs hosted tradeoffs, timeline for POC and benchmarks.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Liam, our performance SE.
[00:07] Riya Kapoor: Hi Maya, hi Liam. Riya here. Thanks for doing this on short notice. We're trying to scope a 6-week pilot to validate inference economics for our triage assistant.
[00:15] Liam Patel: Great — can you give us a bit about constraints? Budget runway, latency needs, any compliance constraints?
[00:22] Sofia Marquez: Sure. Product goal is to replace a rules-based triage with LLM prompts. Target experience: median response <150ms for short prompts (under 256 tokens) and p95 under 300ms, but we're willing to compromise to 250ms p95 as a baseline. Cost wise, we can allocate about $15k/month for the POC phase total.
[00:45] Evan Brooks: Also want to note we have PHI-ish metadata — not full documents but patient-identifying tokens. We need to talk about private deployment and KMS/HSM for keys.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Got it. For PHI we absolutely recommend either Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC and customer-managed KMS. We'll include the SOC2 and our private deployment notes in the pack.
[01:10] Liam Patel: On performance: the win typically comes from three levers — model choice, batching, and caching (prefix / KV cache). For a triage assistant where many prompts share identical headers, KV caching can cut generation tokens significantly.
[01:28] Riya Kapoor: Can you ballpark per-token numbers? We need to map to our $15k budget.
[01:33] Maya Chen: Sure — rough hosted baseline numbers, ballpark: generation token cost around $0.0008/token for similar-sized causal models (this is a hosted list price proxy), and embeddings/indexing costs are separate. With moderate batching and caching we often see effective cost fall to $0.0002–0.0004/token depending on hit rate.
[01:55] Evan Brooks: Hmm, that's a big range. What's driving that gap?
[01:58] Liam Patel: Two things: batching improves GPU utilization — e.g., batching 8–16 can reduce per-token wall time and cost by 1.5–2.5x but pushes latency up if real-time SLOs are tight. Caching (prefix/KV cache) eliminates repeated token generation when prompts are similar; hit rate matters — if you have a 40% cache hit you cut tokens by ~40%. Also quantized models and CPU offloads can change quoted numbers.
[02:25] Sofia Marquez: Our traffic is spiky — weekdays 9–17 heavy, nights low. Peak concurrency expected ~60 concurrent requests across the region, average perhaps 12 qps.
[02:37] Maya Chen: Okay, good to know. For that shape we usually propose a Dedicated pool sized for 95th percentile concurrency with autoscale for bursts, or Hosted with smart routing + burst capacity. For a POC, many customers start hosted to move fast then switch to Dedicated if unit economics require it.
[02:58] Riya Kapoor: Security wise, we need audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC. Can Redwood meet that in hosted?
[03:05] Maya Chen: Yes — hosted supports SSO and audit logs; for KMS and customer key control you would need Dedicated or Private. We'll attach the details.
[03:15] Evan Brooks: Back to numbers — can you walk through a sample cost calc? For example, 100k requests/month average, 600 tokens generated per request, what's the resulting spend?
[03:24] Liam Patel: Quick calc: baseline hosted at $0.0008/token => 100k * 600 * 0.0008 = $48,000 which is above your pilot budget. With batching + cache if effective tokens per request drop to 200 (via 60% cache/hit and some shorter completions) and per-token efficiency improves to $0.0003 => 100k * 200 * 0.0003 = $6,000. So you can see how impactful caching + batching is.
[03:57] Sofia Marquez: That makes sense. What are realistic cache hit rates for triage?
[04:00] Liam Patel: If prompts share templates and only patient data changes in certain slots, we often see 30–60% prefix hits. The trick is to canonicalize prompts — redaction + tokenization helps. Also persistent KV cache across sessions helps warm the cache for common responses.
[04:18] Riya Kapoor: What about latency tradeoffs with batching — we can't add 500ms of wait.
[04:23] Liam Patel: Right. For sub-250ms p95, aggressive batching is hard. You can do small batches like 4–8 with micro-batching (continuous batching) which adds maybe 50–120ms depending on load. If you deploy Dedicated with optimized kernels and quantization, runtime per-token drops and you can preserve latency while batching.
[04:44] Maya Chen: We should run two benchmark types in the POC: 1) latency-focused (to validate p95 under load, small batches), 2) cost-focused (saturated throughput to measure tokens/sec and cost/token with larger batches). We'll also measure cache hit rate using your prompt corpus.
[05:04] Evan Brooks: Excellent. What hardware do you recommend for the Dedicated sizing estimator?
[05:08] Liam Patel: For initial sizing, for the model family you're considering (we discussed an LLaMA-style ~13B variant), one GPU (A100/RTX8000 class) with optimized kernels can sustain X tokens/sec — we'll provide sample numbers in the spreadsheet. For higher concurrency you'd pool more GPUs behind our router. But important: model variant, quantization (8-bit/4-bit), and sequence length distribution change the math.
[05:33] Riya Kapoor: Sequence length — our typical prompt plus history is ~600 tokens, but we can truncate history for MLP. We anticipate average completion length ~150 tokens.
[05:43] Liam Patel: Cool. That helps. We'll parametrize the cost model with average prompt tokens, average completion tokens, cache hit rate, and batch size to generate per-1k-token cost and monthly spend given your QPS.
[05:54] Maya Chen: For the POC timeline, we're proposing: Week 0 (this week) — kickoff, share artifacts; Week 1 — Redwood sends spreadsheet and benchmark harness; Week 2 — Atlas shares traces & prompt set; Week 3 — Redwood runs baseline hosted benchmarks and a dedicated sim in our infra; Weeks 4–5 — joint runs in Atlas staging; Week 6 — final report and recommendation. Does that align with your timelines?
[06:20] Riya Kapoor: Yes, we want results within 6 weeks. Need to ensure legal and security signoffs don't block access to staging.
[06:27] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll get SOC2 + security notes over immediately. Also Redwood can run an initial benchmark in our staging without PHI — using anonymized prompt set — while you complete the legal steps.
[06:40] Evan Brooks: A few technical Qs: can Redwood's KV cache be persisted between sessions? How do we control cache TTLs?
[06:46] Liam Patel: Yes, persistent KV cache is supported. TTLs are configurable per-model route. For the POC we'll recommend a TTL window aligned to your session semantics — e.g., 24–72 hours depending on data sensitivity and churn. And for PHI we can scope what metadata is cached — we can hash identifiers and keep only canonical templates in cache.
[07:06] Sofia Marquez: Any notes on tokenization mismatch and cost surprises? Our engineers worry that different tokenizers can change token counts on user data.
[07:13] Liam Patel: Good point — tokenizer differences matter. We'll run tokenization audits on your prompt corpus to get a distribution and feed that into the model. That will be part of the data you share.
[07:23] Riya Kapoor: If we end up needing Private (air-gapped) deployment, how much timeline slip are we looking at?
[07:28] Maya Chen: Private takes longer — provisioning, on-prem checks, and KMS integration add 4–8 weeks typically. For the POC we'd recommend starting hosted or Dedicated to validate economics, then plan Private as a follow-on if required.
[07:42] Evan Brooks: Can you also show a scenario where we keep a small Dedicated pool for latency-critical endpoints and route bulk/long-running tasks to hosted cheaper variants?
[07:50] Liam Patel: Absolutely — hybrid routing is common: latency-critical subset pinned to Dedicated low-latency route, bulk/analytics routed to lower-cost instances. We'll model a split scenario in the spreadsheet.
[07:59] Sofia Marquez: On observability — we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards. Does Redwood expose that?
[08:05] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Console includes token-level cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks, and the ability to tag requests. We'll attach screenshots to the packet.
[08:15] Riya Kapoor: Great. Anything else we should prepare on our side?
[08:19] Maya Chen: Prompt set, anonymized traffic logs, target SLOs prioritized, and any onboarding constraints for security team. Also a list of any models you're already evaluating.
[08:27] Evan Brooks: We'll get those by Friday.
[08:29] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll send the spreadsheet and harness early next week.
[08:33] (brief cross-talk)
[08:36] Liam Patel: Quick sample numbers I'll include in the spreadsheet: - Baseline hosted cost: $0.0008 / gen token - Effective with caching & batching: $0.0002–0.0004 / gen token - Small-batch latency penalty: +50–120ms at low qps - Batch of 8 yields roughly 1.8x perf improvement in tokens/sec for 13B quantized models (approx)
[08:57] Riya Kapoor: Good, that's actionable.
[09:00] Sofia Marquez: One last question — do you support auto-fallback to a cheaper model on overload?
[09:05] Maya Chen: Yes, routing policies can fallback to smaller model variants or to a best-effort replica. We can set percentage rollouts and automatic fallbacks by latency/cost thresholds.
[09:18] Evan Brooks: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the spreadsheet.
[09:22] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll recap via email and post the artifacts.

Recap / agreed success criteria:
- Validate p95 latency target <250ms for defined short prompt flows (latency benchmark).
- Demonstrate effective unit cost <= $0.0004/gen-token with realistic batching & caching assumptions (cost benchmark).
- Provide Dedicated sizing estimate and a hybrid routing plan if needed.
- Deliver final POC report with costs, latency, and recommended rollout by end of week 6.

Shared artifacts referenced: cost-model-template.xlsx (link), benchmark-harness repo (link), SOC2_security_pack.pdf (link)
